# Raincloud plots for all motif annotations

The figure shows half violins, white box plots and all observations, using pink for motif perturbations and gray for matched backgrounds. Positive and negative patterns are separated across pages; each page contains at most four motifs and one background. All 11 labels and 16 annotation/sign combinations are retained with a common full-range axis.

Effects are WT minus disrupted predictions in original PC1 units. Points are averaged by positive DNA-overlap group. Displayed backgrounds are deduplicated by match_id and then averaged by source DNA group; inference still uses the original one-to-one matched pairs. Shared motif annotations do not provide independent evidence for distinct proteins. raincloud_plot_values.tsv contains the plotted values and all_motifs_summary.tsv contains the original summary statistics.

For offline plotting, place plot_all_raincloud.py, final_figure_small.py, tf_annotation_effects.tsv and tf_statistics.tsv together, install numpy, pandas and matplotlib, and run python plot_all_raincloud.py. The frozen-data redraw does not require model inference.

# Motif panels with a magnified effect axis

The common range is -0.0015 to +0.0015 PC1 with 0.0005 ticks, displayed at 1e-3 scale. Five pages cover all 11 annotations, with positive and negative patterns separated. Stars indicate the original exploratory annotation/sign pooled Holm-adjusted thresholds: 0.05 and 0.01. Each group was compared with its own one-to-one matched background. Points are source-DNA-group averages; they have no individual P values. None of the 44 primary pattern tests passed correction, and shared annotations do not establish independent protein identities. Boundary triangles mark clipped display values; all data and original tests remain available. significance_and_outside_range.tsv records exact P values and clipping counts.

# Compact motif panel with a fixed display range

The 8 by 2.5 inch canvas shows KLF16, SP1, SP2, SP4 and matched backgrounds. Effects are WT minus disrupted PC1, displayed at 1e-3 scale over +/-0.002 with 0.001 ticks. Values outside the axis limits remain in the data; boundary triangles indicate clipping. All observations are retained without sampling. Significance stars are disabled. The exploratory annotation groups can share patterns; the original one-to-one matched tests and their Holm corrections are unchanged.

Repeat labels use the shortest observed run in each partition. The two T-rich branches have run lengths 14/5/5 and 18/15/13 and are labeled 5T+ and 13T+. Reverse-complement orientation is used for A-rich members. The plus sign indicates longer observed runs and is not a significance marker. Shared labels do not establish distinct TF families. Mixed cores retain supported contiguous IUPAC features; noncontiguous runs are not joined. Independent-pattern stars identify individual patterns rather than significance. Blue/pink branches indicate negative/positive PC1 attribution, gray sectors indicate partitions and outer-ring purple indicates match status. Partition cores use 4-12-bp descriptive rules; independent patterns use six-base windows.

# Gene feature groups

This directory regroups existing cleaned features without recalculating, normalizing or imputing values.

| Group | Description | Predictors |
|---|---|---:|
| B | Basic gene architecture | 22 |
| Q | Sequence composition, GC and local CpG | 13 |
| I | CpG-island annotations | 8 |
| C | CDS codon frequencies | 61 |
| P | Pausing-region 1-4-mer frequencies | 340 |
| E | Gene-body 1-4-mer frequencies | 340 |
| T | Predicted CTCF binding | 2 |

gene identifies rows and Y_PC1 is the response. Neither is a predictor. Transcript, chromosome, strand, TSS, TES and biotype fields remain annotation metadata. feature_dictionary_long.tsv records group membership; validation_summary.tsv records row counts, feature counts and missing values.

# Full-range compact motif panel

The 8 by 2.5 inch canvas shows KLF16, SP1, SP2, SP4 and their matched background as half violins, white boxes and all 1453 observations. The range is +/-0.005 PC1 with 0.002 major ticks, displayed at 1e-3 scale. Tick labels are 12 pt and axis labels are 14 pt. All observations are shown, without sampling, clipping markers or significance stars. The annotation groups can share sequence patterns. This operation changes presentation only; model predictions and the original matched statistical tests are retained.

. The figure and final 101-bp mutagenesis example use the same gene and fold-10 seqlet. Values are signed PC1 contributions. Complete input positions are 0-599; the source seqlet spans 55-104 and the SP4-like match spans 96-104. Contributions are observed-base one-hot values multiplied by five-seed mean hypothetical attributions, without smoothing or normalization. This is one seqlet, not the 98-seqlet average pattern. Frozen data, coordinates and source hashes are retained.

- `analysis/paper_style_naming_matched44.tsv`: 44 matched patterns, original identifiers, annotations and core coordinates.
- `analysis/paper_style_naming_members65.tsv`: 65 partition members.
- `analysis/paper_style_naming_TOMTOM79.tsv`: 79 retained database matches.
- `analysis/paper_style_naming_QA.json`: naming parameters and records.

# Compact motif panel

The 8 by 2.5 inch canvas contains half violins, white boxes and all observations. Pink marks the four exploratory positive-annotation groups and gray marks matched backgrounds. Tick labels are 12 pt and axis labels are 14 pt. Effects are WT minus disrupted PC1, shown at 1e-3 scale. The displayed range is +/-0.0015 with 0.0005 ticks; boundary triangles indicate values outside the display range. All values remain in the data. Significance stars, when enabled, describe the original annotation/sign pooled tests with Holm-adjusted thresholds of 0.05 and 0.01. Tests use each group's matched background, not the pooled gray display distribution. The --no-stars option removes stars. No model inference or statistical recalculation is performed.

# Unified A/T-rich sequence annotation

The two T-rich partitions share a poly(A/T) feature label, 5T+, connected to their original branches by annotation brackets. The clustering topology and all 29 shaded regions are retained. Their six oriented T-run lengths are 14, 5, 5, 18, 15 and 13. The shared label represents a lower bound rather than mutually exclusive biological families. Independent-pattern stars retain their original descriptive meaning. Member identifiers, lengths, database annotations and orientations are recorded in the associated tables.

# Compact motif panels without significance stars

All 11 TF annotations and 16 annotation/sign combinations are shown. Positive and negative attribution patterns have separate rows and matched backgrounds. The zoomed PDF uses +/-0.0015 PC1 with 0.0005 ticks and boundary markers; the full-range PDF retains all points. The canvas is 10.8 by 5.4 inches, with 12 pt ticks, 14 pt axis labels and editable PDF text. Effects are WT minus disrupted PC1 in original units, displayed at 1e-3 scale. TF annotations can share patterns. Missing annotation/sign combinations are not replaced by zeros. Statistics are unchanged.

# Figure 5 resources

Four packages contain the complete ZBTB7A TSS attribution, circular motif tree, SP4 alignment and 101-bp mutagenesis panel. Each provides a PDF, plotting code, data, provenance and hashes. Run python plot_all.py to redraw them sequentially. Frozen values and upstream experiments are retained.

# Exploratory significant-annotation panel

This display includes the positive-pattern annotation groups KLF16, SP1, SP2 and SP4, which passed the original pooled Holm-adjusted 0.05 threshold, together with their matched backgrounds. Shared underlying patterns make these groups statistically dependent; all 44 primary pattern-level tests remained nonsignificant after correction. The range is +/-0.0015 PC1 with 0.0005 ticks, displayed at 1e-3 scale. Boundary triangles indicate out-of-range values retained in plot_values.tsv. No tests are recalculated.

NascentAtlas interface figures

Six individual PDFs and a six-page composite are provided. Each page is approximately 180 mm wide with a 4252-pixel screenshot at an effective 600 dpi. Screenshots were captured at fourfold browser pixel density and downsampled. PI views retain complete rows; the gene-feature view shows all 30 features. URLs, pixel dimensions, effective resolution and hashes are recorded in figure_manifest.json.
Allowed bases need not have equal probabilities. Full probabilities remain in the source matrices. IUPAC definitions and the consensus rule follow the documented Biopython implementation.
Retained matches use q<=0.05 and overlap>=5 bp. A q value describes false-discovery-rate significance, not a TF-binding probability.

The same ZBTB7A instance: input positions 50-150, SP4-like match 96-104 and C-to-G substitution at 99. Gain/loss curves summarize five-seed substitution extrema with Gaussian sigma=1.1 bp; the heatmap is unsmoothed. Units are delta Y_PC1.

Runs of at least three identical bases use count-plus-base notation: 6T=TTTTTT, 5TA=TTTTTA and CN3GN=CNGGGN. Suffixes distinguish patterns sharing a short label; they do not indicate significance or separate TF families.

# Sequence-based partition labels

The original 314-pattern tree, 13 partitions and 16 independent items are retained. Labels summarize IUPAC cores and repeat lengths without changing tree membership.

## Repeat labels

The 44 matched sequence patterns have unique display names representing 29 distinct six-base sequence features. These labels do not establish 29 validated biological motif families. The 79 qualifying TOMTOM matches and 11 JASPAR matrices are retained.

Labels summarize the highest-information contiguous six-base window of the original full-precision 50-bp probability matrix using IUPAC consensus. They are short sequence features, not complete patterns or guaranteed TOMTOM alignment intervals.
